title: Naan-style flatbread
summary: Soft, blistered skillet flatbreads made with yogurt, brushed with garlic butter.
steps: Whisk the almond flour, coconut flour, psyllium, baking powder and salt.
Stir in the yogurt, warm water and olive oil and knead briefly into a soft dough. Cover and rest 10 minutes.
Divide into 6 and roll each between two sheets of parchment into an oval about 3 mm (⅛ in) thick.
Heat a dry cast-iron pan over medium-high heat. Peel off the top sheet, flip a flatbread into the pan and peel off the second sheet.
Cook 1½–2 minutes per side, until blistered and spotted brown.
Mix the melted butter with the garlic and brush over the hot flatbreads.
dairy_free_notes: Coconut yogurt is thinner than Greek yogurt; hold back a tablespoon of the water and add it only if the dough feels stiff.
tips: Psyllium gives this dough a bread-like chew; brands differ, and some darken the crumb purple-grey — it is harmless.

origin.history: Naan is a leavened flatbread of South and Central Asia, traditionally slapped onto the wall of a clay tandoor oven. It is recorded at the courts of medieval Delhi, and today is closely associated with the cooking of northern India and Pakistan.
